report_name: SideCopy APT Expands Targeting to Indian Academic Institutions

threat_actors.name: SideCopy
threat_actors.description: A Pakistan-nexus advanced persistent threat (APT) group that has expanded its targeting from Indian government and military entities to include academic institutions. The group is known for mimicking the TTPs of the Sidewinder group.
threat_actors.goals: Espionage and intelligence collection against India, with a new focus on academic institutions for research, intellectual property, or compromising individuals with government ties.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: Used for initial access by delivering a ZIP archive containing a malicious LNK file via a spear-phishing email.

attack_patterns.name: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: A malicious LNK file with a .docx.lnk extension and a PDF icon was used to deceive the user into initiating the infection chain.

attack_patterns.name: Mshta
attack_patterns.description: The malicious LNK file invoked mshta.exe to download and execute an obfuscated HTML Application (HTA) file from a remote server.

attack_patterns.name: Reflective Code Loading
attack_patterns.description: The initial HTA script reflectively loaded a dropper DLL into memory to evade disk-based detection and hinder forensic analysis.

attack_patterns.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: A batch script created a persistence mechanism by adding a Run Key in 'HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' to execute a secondary HTA file on system startup.

attack_patterns.name: Template Injection
attack_patterns.description: A secondary HTA script reconstructed a XAML payload which then leveraged .NET deserialization to reflectively load the final ReverseRAT payload into memory.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The ReverseRAT backdoor used web protocols to communicate with its C2 server, with the traffic being encrypted with a hard-coded AES key.

malware.name: ReverseRAT
malware.description: A .NET-based RAT delivered as the final payload in a multi-stage attack. It is loaded reflectively into memory using .NET deserialization and provides capabilities like file exfiltration, command execution, and screen capture.

tools.name: Mshta
tools.description: Used to download and execute a remote, obfuscated HTA file from a malicious server as part of the initial execution and staging phase.

identities.name: Indian academic institutions
identities.description: A new target sector for the SideCopy APT group, targeted via spear-phishing to deploy ReverseRAT for espionage purposes.

identities.name: Trellix
identities.description: The security vendor that analyzed and reported on the SideCopy campaign.

infrastructure.name: SideCopy HTA Payload Server
infrastructure.description: Remote server at docsportal[.]in used to host the initial malicious HTA file for the SideCopy campaign.

infrastructure.name: ReverseRAT C2 Server
infrastructure.description: C2 server at dns.educationportals[.]biz used by the ReverseRAT payload. The domain is a reused asset associated with SideCopy.

indicators.name: SideCopy APT C2 and Payload Domains
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: SideCopy APT C2 and Payload Domains DNS Query
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries to domains associated with the SideCopy APT group's campaign targeting Indian academic institutions.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/sidecopy-broadens-india-targeting-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: high
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - '.docsportal.in'
      - '.educationportals.biz'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to known malicious domains used by SideCopy for payload delivery and command and control.

indicators.name: Suspicious Remote HTA Execution via Mshta
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Remote HTA Execution via Mshta
id: e2b3c4d5-f6a7-4891-8cde-f12345678901
status: experimental
description: Detects mshta.exe being used to execute a remote HTA file, a technique used by SideCopy and other threat actors.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/sidecopy-broadens-india-targeting-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1218.005
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of mshta.exe with a URL as a command-line argument, a TTP used by SideCopy to download remote payloads.

indicators.name: Disguised LNK File Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Disguised LNK File Creation
id: d3c4e5f6-a7b8-4012-8def-123456789012
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of LNK files with double extensions, a common phishing technique used by SideCopy.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/sidecopy-broadens-india-targeting-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '.docx.lnk'
      - '.pdf.lnk'
      - '.xlsx.lnk'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of files with double extensions, such as `.docx.lnk`, which is a classic phishing lure used by SideCopy.

indicators.name: Suspicious HTA Persistence in Run Key
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious HTA Persistence in Run Key
id: c4d5e6f7-b8c9-4123-8f01-345678901234
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a registry run key that points to an HTA file, a persistence technique used by SideCopy.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/sidecopy-broadens-india-targeting-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-22
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    EventType: 'SetValue'
    TargetObject|contains: '\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
    Details|endswith: '.hta'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a registry Run Key pointing to an HTA file, a persistence method used by SideCopy in this campaign.
